references.text: Moses urges the people to bring gifts for the sanctuary, which is the reason the people must now be stopped from giving more.
Describes the people's generous response to Moses' call to bring materials for the tabernacle, resulting in an abundance.
The immediate context explaining why Moses had to issue this command—the craftsmen reported that the people were bringing more than was needed.
The Lord's original instruction to Moses to collect gifts from the people for the sanctuary.
Paul describes the churches in Macedonia who gave beyond their means of their own free will, a similar example of overwhelming generosity among God's people.
The principle of voluntary and joyful giving, reflecting the attitude of the Israelites who contributed to the tabernacle.
Hebrews confirms that the construction of the tabernacle (where giving was stopped in Ex 36) followed a heavenly pattern.
Both verses illustrate the principle that the people must respect God's set boundaries to preserve holiness.
